item.description: A Technical Community post discusses the topic of using the Entra ID continuous access evaluation (CAE) feature to revoke access for service principals when apps become risky or potentially compromised. The Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools app is a good example of a service principal in common use, so we examine the access tokens issued for interactive Graph sessions to discover if they are CAE-enabled. item.title: Why Microsoft Graph Does Not Support Group Mailboxes
item.description: A reader asked why the Outlook Mail Graph API doesn't support access to group mailboxes. The basic reason is that a group mailbox doesn't have an account and the Outlook Mail API only supports mailboxes that are linked to an account. When you look at the current usage of group mailboxes, it doesn’t seem like there’s much data to mine. Maybe the need for Graph API support for group mailboxes isn’t such a big thing?...

item.title: Microsoft 365 Groups, Conversations, Threads, and Posts
item.description: When launched in 2015, Outlook groups were an email-based collaboration platform. Now called Microsoft 365 Groups, the few Outlook groups that host email-based discussions have a distinctive Graph API to create and manage the conversations, topics, and posts which make up their discussions. This article reviews how to fetch these objects and how to create new conversations and reply to posts (using the Outlook Groups APIs, of course)....

September’s Intune updates help more government organizations use advanced management capabilities while giving IT teams greater control over change. item.title: Action Required: Upgrade ExchangeOnlineManagement PowerShell Module to Version 3.10.1 or Newer
item.description:
We have introduced security enhancements to Exchange Online PowerShell authentication in ExchangeOnlineManagement module version 3.10.1 and newer. These enhancements strengthen the authentication flow and provide additional protection against emerging threats.
Customers using a version earlier than 3.10.1 should upgrade to version 3.10.1 or later. Exchange Online authentication will increasingly rely on the security enhancements available in these versions, and older module versions may not support future authentication requirements. item.title: EWS Deprecation Is Here – What This Means To You
item.description: The deprecation of EWS in Exchange Online starts today. This is a multi-step process, years in the making, and this post has lots of important information.
